gaps.sentence: She was on the verge of ___ up her job to sail around the world.
gaps.explanation: 'On the verge of' ends in a preposition, so the gerund follows.

gaps.sentence: Instead of ___ , why don't you ask for help?
She would rather ___ at home tonight.
gaps.explanation: 'Would rather do' — the bare infinitive follows.

gaps.sentence: I didn't mean ___ you — it was a joke.
gaps.explanation: mean (= intend) takes the to-infinitive: didn't mean to upset. (mean + -ing = involve.)

gaps.sentence: My parents wouldn't let me ___ out past midnight.
gaps.explanation: 'Let someone do' — 'let' takes the bare infinitive.
can't stand + -ing (also to-infinitive in AmE): can't stand waiting. -ing accepted as standard.

gaps.sentence: He apologised for ___ so rude to the waiter.
gaps.explanation: 'Apologise for being' — 'for' is a preposition, so the gerund follows.
fail takes the to-infinitive: failed to meet.
